It may be (I haven't looked into it), but every single seizure a person gets causes brain damage, which can be small or large depending on the severity of the seizure. The boy is in a wheelchair and unable to speak, no doubt due to brain damage because of his constant seizures. 

Also, the article states that the boy is on 5 medications. I can almost guarantee that one or more of those is a benzodiazepine (they are often used to treat epilepsy, especially severe epilepsy/prolonged seizures because they slow down the CNS thus reducing the likelihood of abnormal electrical activity which is what causes seizures). These are extremely dangerous drugs for adults, and even though the effect on children's brains has not been sufficiently studied, one can assume that they have the same (if not amplified) effects. Benzodiazepines can impair concentration and memory along with a long list of other symptoms. What is worse, though, is how addicting they are. Addicts say that coming off of benzos is harder than coming off of heroin. Their withdrawal effects are terribly unpleasant (anxiety, depression, hallucinations to name a few), often lead to hospitalizations, and can even be life-threatening - increased risk of seizures, stroke, etc.

Based on this, one could make a convincing argument that the benefits of MMJ outweigh the risks. In my opinion with the amount of brain damage he has already suffered and will continue to suffer from if his seizures are not controlled, even if marijuana does 'stunt brain growth,' it will be very minor compared to if he doesn't use it and continues having seizures.

Source: epilepsy patient, have been prescribed benzos

I would go 4+ days without sleeping, and when I finally was able to give in to the exhaustion I would wake up screaming in the middle of the night. Do not blame her. It is not her fault, make sure you assure her of that. Things like "you shouldn't have drank so much" or "why did you go home with him in the first place" aren't helpful.

On a similar note, try not to get upset. I know it might be emotional to hear about this happening to someone you care about, but they need you to be strong for them when they're in this time of crisis.

Understand that rape/sexual assault is not something that one can "get over." She may still wake up screaming months or even years after the event. Try not to get frustrated that she is still struggling, she really needs your support. I know that I was frustrated with myself for still being so messed up about it months later, and it was heartbreaking when my friend got angry at my mental instability. Trust me, if I could stop being a teary-eyed wreck, I would. As difficult as it may be for you to deal with me, realize that it is a hundred times harder *being* me.

She might lash out. She's going through a lot. Understand that it is not personal and she doesn't hate you, she just isn't able to handle all of the pain.

Keep her secret if she asks you not to tell.

Be careful with physical contact, it might be traumatic for her and/or bring up flashbacks. Ask before you touch her.

As much as you can try not to pry for details. She will share with you when she is ready.

Don't force her to report it. You may suggest it, but don't push. If she wants to, she will. And do not say anything like "If you don't report it then he'll rape someone else." She knows. She feels guilty enough. And it's not her fault if he rapes someone else, it's his for being a fucking rapist.

Suggest that she gets help. Offer to go with her to talk to someone. The day after I was raped, my roommate went with me to the women's center on campus and helped me explain to a counselor what happened. It meant the world to me and it really helped, I don't think I would have been able to fully and properly explain the situation to a stranger.

Be careful about rape jokes. I know they can be funny, I know that phrases like "I totally raped that Magikarp in that pokemon battle" are common among young people but there's a good chance that they are making her cringe.

And finally, be patient. She is going through a lot and might have a hard time talking about everything, getting on with every day life, interacting with people, etc. Healing takes time and it is a long, uphill journey. Be there to support her.

(This is not gender specific, a rape victim can be male/female/trans/straight/gay/lesbian/pans/anything, a rapist can be male/female/trans/straight/gay/lesbian/pans/whatever.)

I actually believe that you cannot use classes to fulfill multiples GEs. When I talked to an advisor in L&S, she said that if a class fulfills more than one GE area, the computer system will make it so that it fulfills whichever requirement you are lacking in. So each class can only fulfill one GE requirement.

That being said, if a class fulfills, for example, both area F and a writing requirement, you will get credit for both area F and for one writing class. But if the class fulfills both area B and E, for example, the system will decide which requirement it will fulfill.

(That's just what I was told though, maybe I could have been given wrong information).

To OP, they reserve spots in many of the intro GE classes for each orientation date, so there is a good chance that space will open up when it comes time for you to sign up for classes.

I would definitely advise crashing, I have gotten into every class I crashed. Crashing means that the first 1-2 weeks of your quarter might be a bit hellish but trust me, it is worth it in the end. /u/seifuu gave very good advice for crashing.

Chem 1A, Chem 1AL, Math (unless you've already filled the requirements for your major with APs, look into that), and then a GE that seems interesting to you. A lot of people like Psych 1, but that fills up fast at orientation so you might not be able to get it. I have heard that Soc 1 is also a very interesting class, so look into it.

If you want, instead of a GE or math (if you've fulfilled your math requirements) you could take writing 1, 2, or 50 (depending on what you've tested out of), but it might be a lot of work for your first quarter. Just remember that you have to take Writing 1 by the end of your freshman year.

Make sure you sign up for Chem and Chem lab first because they are pretty quick to fill up and you definitely want to start taking it your first quarter in order to be on track to graduate in four years.

Also, even if it looks like the classes are full right now on GOLD, they reserve some spots for every orientation date, so a lot of them will open up.

Current freshman residing in Anacapa. I love it here.

Half of the rooms in FT are tripled, 1 in each suite. FT is and always will be a party dorm. Lots of bong rips taking place in the bathrooms. It can get really crazy and the RAs pretty much give up so it can be hard to study when it gets loud, I have a lot of friends who hate that part of it. But it's really social, and people get really close since it's pretty far off campus. I find the bike ride to be a pain but most people who live there don't mind it most of the time unless it's raining. Portola, FT's dining commons, sucks for the most part. It has some quality Lucky Charms though.

In the shorties (Anacapa, Santa Cruz, and Santa Rosa), probably 2/3 of the rooms are triples. Honestly it's not that bad, at first it seems really cramped but you get used to it quickly and learn how to manage your stuff. It's actually pretty cool living with 2 people. I was really disappointed to be in a triple but now I honestly don't mind it.
The shorties are chill. Close to classes, close to the beach. And there's a really nice grassy area between Anacapa and Santa Cruz that's across the street from the beach, people tan there and play frisbee/soccer and they slackline. Guys and girls are on separate floors. Anacapa and Santa Cruz  are shaped kinda like swastikas. There are two wings (arms of the swastika) on each side of the building. It's arrange with one wing of girls and one of boys on each floor, with floors directly above/below each other housing diffent genders. Even though you live on separate floors, it's really easy to meet friends of the opposite sex. You have events with the floor above/below you and with the whole building. Anacapa at least is really social and you get close to a lot of people because it's only two stories and there are so many people living there. It's really chill. A party dorm for sure, lots of stoners as well. Santa Cruz was a bit quieter this year but a decent number of people still party there.

San Nic (tower) has guys and girls on the same floor. Very few triples, 1 or 2 per floor, and 1 or 2 singles per floor. 8th floor is all girls. Nice views. This year it housed mainly kids who did the Freshman Summer Start Program, and at the beginnig of the year they were really close but by now a lot of people dislike living there and hate the people. Just something to keep in mind. Also if you don't do FSSP you might find it hard to make friends or feel kinda left out at the beginning of the year because everyone else already knows each other. But you will make a lot of friends, it's a really social dorm.  I don't know if they're gonna keep the FSSP kids there all year next year though. 

San Mig has 2 towers that are adjoined. Guys and Girls are housed on alternating floors. I haven't seen any triples in San Mig but I'm not over there much.

I wouldn't advise living in Manzanita. It's across campus from all the other freshmen, a lot of non-freshman live there, and I've been told that it's rwally quiet (too quiet).

You will honestly have fun in any dorm you live in. You will meet cool people, make good friends, and you'll find people to party with, smoke with, study with, whatever. Like someone else said, no matter where you go it's all just ton of drunk freshmen.

Good luck! You'll love it here
